samples.summary: DOCX table-cell `w:fill` still interpolates an untrusted color string unescaped — bypasses the XML escaping this delta added to run properties
samples.evidence: The delta closes attribute injection for `<w:color>` / `<w:shd w:fill>` inside `buildRunPropertiesXml` (packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:78-84). The very same OOXML attribute is written for table cells without any escaping: `packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:309-311` — `const hex = cell.style.backgroundColor.replace('#', ''); tcPrParts.push(`<w:shd w:val="clear" w:color="auto" w:fill="${hex}"/>`)`. `CellStyle.backgroundColor` is a plain `string` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:441) fed from untrusted input: the DOCX importer builds it verbatim from the source file's `w:fill` attribute (`packages/docs/src/import/docx-style-map.ts:174`: `result.backgroundColor = `#${fill}``, and docx-importer.ts:431 copies it onto the cell), and HTML paste writes `td.style.backgroundColor` (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:417). Import → export round-trip therefore emits e.g. `w:fill="a"/><w:b"`, breaking the element / injecting OOXML in the exported document (also reachable from the CLI export path, packages/cli/src/docs/docx-export.ts). Fix belongs on docx-exporter.ts:310 (reuse `escapeXmlAttr`, ideally exported from docx-style-map.ts).

The very same OOXML attribute is written for table cells without any escaping: `packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:309-311` — `const hex = cell.style.backgroundColor.replace('#', ''); tcPrParts.push(`<w:shd w:val="clear" w:color="auto" w:fill="${hex}"/>`)`. `CellStyle.backgroundColor` is a plain `string` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:441) fed from untrusted input: the DOCX importer builds it verbatim from the source file's `w:fill` attribute (`packages/docs/src/import/docx-style-map.ts:174`: `result.backgroundColor = `#${fill}``, and docx-importer.ts:431 copies it onto the cell), and HTML paste writes `td.style.backgroundColor` (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:417). verdict.reason: Every claimed fact checks out. The delta's guard is real and module-private: `escapeXmlAttr` at packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:25-32 is applied to the run-level `<w:shd w:fill>` at docx-style-map.ts:81-85 and `<w:color>` at :79. The bypassing writer is present verbatim at packages/docs/src/export/docx-exporter.ts:309-311, emitting the same `w:fill` attribute from `cell.style.backgroundColor.replace('#','')` with no escaping (neighbouring tcPr attributes at :306-307 are numeric, so this is the sole string-valued one). The value is untrusted and never validated: CellStyle.backgroundColor is a raw `string` (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:441, unlike the StoredColor at :180 on the run path); the importer builds it verbatim from the source file's attribute (packages/docs/src/import/docx-style-map.ts:171-175 via the unsanitized getWAttr at :11-13) and copies it onto the cell (packages/docs/src/import/docx-importer.ts:427-438). A grep for isHexColor|sanitizeColor|validateColor across packages/docs/src returned no matches, so no guard elsewhere makes this unreachable. The import->export round trip is reachable outside the browser too (packages/cli/src/docs/docx-import.ts:74 -> packages/cli/src/docs/docx-export.ts:33), and HTML paste also writes the field (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:417,497). This is in-lane for blast-radius (a second writer of the attribute the diff just hardened, reached via a different entry point and invisible in the diff) and major impact: a hostile fill value breaks the <w:shd> element / injects OOXML into the exported document.

finding.summary: Table-cell text still paints legacy `color: ''` through `??`, so the #728 stale-fillStyle bug survives inside tables
finding.evidence: `packages/docs/src/view/table-renderer.ts:457` — `const runTextColor = defaultColorResolver(style.color) ?? Theme.defaultColor;` and `:564` — `ctx.fillStyle = defaultColorResolver(cellBlock.inlines[0]?.style.color) ?? Theme.defaultColor;`. Table blocks never go through `renderRun` (paint-layout skips `block.type === 'table'` at lines 221 and 277; table-renderer does its own `ctx.font`/`ctx.fillStyle`/`ctx.fillText` at 451-483 and the list-marker path at 558-565). `defaultColorResolver` returns strings verbatim (`packages/docs/src/model/color.ts:16`), so a stored `color: ''` yields `''`, `ctx.fillStyle = ''` is ignored by the canvas, and the run keeps whatever the previous pass set — the table content pass runs *after* the selection layer (see the comment at table-renderer.ts:471-474 and the explicit `ctx.fillStyle = focused ? Theme.selectionColor : ...` at :442). The task doc for this change explicitly declines a data migration (docs/tasks/active/20260812-docs-font-color-reset-todo.md:51-52), so already-saved `''` values are the intended coverage of the renderer guard — and text in tables is not covered. Fix belongs in table-renderer.ts:457/564 (`|| Theme.defaultColor`).

verdict.reason: The claimed code is not present. Both table text-paint sites already route through the #728 guard, not a bare `??` on `defaultColorResolver`: `table-renderer.ts:463-465` uses `resolveStoredColor(defaultColorResolver, style.color) ?? Theme.defaultColor` for cell text (with a comment at :457-462 naming the paint-layout table skip as the reason), and `table-renderer.ts:571-574` uses the same helper for the in-cell list marker. `resolveStoredColor` (model/color.ts:45-50) collapses `''` to `undefined` before the resolver and applies `|| undefined` after, so a stored `color: ''` resolves to `undefined` and falls back to `Theme.defaultColor`; `''` cannot reach `ctx.fillStyle` on either path. The file's only remaining raw `defaultColorResolver` calls are background fills that are truthiness-gated (`:176` `if (cellBg)`, `:225` `if (!bg) continue;`), so they cannot paint `''` either. The cited task doc in fact records the table-renderer cell text + in-cell marker guard as completed (20260812-docs-font-color-reset-todo.md:42-46) with tests (:60-62), contradicting the finding's premise that tables were left uncovered. No bypassing site exists.
